alerts.title: Uncontrolled Hypothyroidism
alerts.message: The patient has symptoms and lab findings of uncontrolled hypothyroidism (TSH 12.4 mIU/L, low free T4, weight gain, fatigue, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, delayed reflexes). This is a significant non-drug cause for the reported weight gain and metabolic symptoms. The clinician's plan to continue the same levothyroxine dose without adjustment does not address this. While DTG is associated with weight gain, the guideline states the association may not be causal and could reflect less metabolic toxicity compared to older regimens.

evidence.recommended_action: Adjust levothyroxine dose to treat hypothyroidism before attributing weight gain solely to DTG.

alerts.title: Dyslipidemia Needs Management
alerts.message: Patient has dyslipidemia with elevated LDL (4.2 mmol/L), total cholesterol (6.4 mmol/L), and triglycerides (2.3 mmol/L). This increases cardiovascular risk. The clinician's plan does not address lipid management. While DTG can be associated with weight gain, the guideline suggests this may reflect less metabolic toxicity from older ART. The uncontrolled hypothyroidism is also a contributing factor to dyslipidemia.

evidence.recommended_action: Address dyslipidemia per cardiovascular risk guidelines and manage contributing hypothyroidism.

alerts.title: Viral Load Monitoring Overdue
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend checking viral load every 6 months for patients on DTG-based ART, or every 12 months if VL has been <50 copies/mL for over a year with reliable adherence. The patient's last viral load was 106 days ago (over 3 months) and was <50 copies/mL. The clinician's plan does not include scheduling the next viral load test.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule next viral load test as per monitoring frequency guidelines (6 or 12 monthly).

alerts.title: Consider Hyperglycemia Risk Factors
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend checking glucose for patients with 2 or more risk factors for hyperglycemia when initiating ART or transitioning to DTG. This patient has multiple risk factors: age >=30 years, BMI >=25 kg/m2 (currently 33), and hypertension may be a risk factor based on borderline BP. Fasting glucose today is normal (5.6 mmol/L).

evidence.recommended_action: Continue monitoring glucose periodically given persistent risk factors (age, high BMI).
